newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St George says profit difficult to repeat.
newsitem.headline: St George says profit difficult to repeat.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it would be hard to repeat its first half profit performance due to pressure on its margins from repeated interest rate cuts.
"The interim results were very satisfactory in all the circumstances," managing director Jim Sweeney said.

"The ability to pay a fully franked dividend of 26 cents - with the preessure of the merger and interest rate reductions - was certainly pleasing. However, continued downward pressure on interest rates and, therefore, greater margin contraction, will make it difficult to repeat the effort in the second half of the year," he said in a newsletter to shareholders.

The bank completed its A$2.6 billion takeover of rival Sydney-based regional bank Advance Bank Ltd earlier this year. Both banks have large mortgage-based books, hence their depiction as regional banks, and the combined group ranks as the fifth largest bank in Australia.
The four major banks have larger books with stronger business exposures and a branch network in each state and territory.

"Competition for asset-based financing is tougher today than it has ever been. The balance sheet pressure brought to bear by the larger banks and the cherrypicking by the mortgage originators is producing an intensely competitive environment," Sweeney said.
He also said the bank wanted to have a more aggressive presence in Queensland and Victoria.
"Our market strategy will reflect this in the coming months," Sweeney said.

The bank achieved a sharp rise in first half net profit to A$99.74 million from A$74.52 million, with the result in the latest six months to March 31 including an inaugural A$19.1 million contribution from Advance.
